chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: In JavaScript, the call, apply, and bind methods can be used to assign an object to the this

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: keyword.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: Take a look at this object.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: We have three properties.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: First name, last name, and full name.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: Full name is a function that returns the concatenated first and last names.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: Here, the this keyword refers to the person object.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: In this example, we have multiple person objects.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: By using call, we can set the this value.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: The first argument is the object being assigned.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: Then we can pass in more arguments.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: These will then be used by the function.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: This time, our function has two parameters.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: We can assign our object, then provide our two arguments.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: The apply method is similar to the call method.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: The only difference is that the call method takes arguments separately, and the apply

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: method takes arguments as an array.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: So when working with arrays, you would want to use apply.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: There are other interesting things that you can do with apply.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: For instance, JavaScript arrays do not have a max method.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: So if we have an array of numbers, and we want to get the maximum value, we could use

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: apply.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: Here, we are not assigning anything to the this keyword.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: So we just set that to null, then pass in our array.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: The bind method creates a new bound function, which wraps the original function object.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: So here we are essentially creating a new function bound to the object.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: Then we call the function along with our arguments.

chunks.title: JavaScript call() apply() bind() Methods
chunks.text: This has been a 90-second JavaScript January.

text: In JavaScript, the call, apply, and bind methods can be used to assign an object to the this keyword. Take a look at this object. We have three properties. First name, last name, and full name. Full name is a function that returns the concatenated first and last names. Here, the this keyword refers to the person object. In this example, we have multiple person objects. By using call, we can set the this value. The first argument is the object being assigned. Then we can pass in more arguments. These will then be used by the function. This time, our function has two parameters. We can assign our object, then provide our two arguments. The apply method is similar to the call method. The only difference is that the call method takes arguments separately, and the apply method takes arguments as an array. So when working with arrays, you would want to use apply. There are other interesting things that you can do with apply. For instance, JavaScript arrays do not have a max method. So if we have an array of numbers, and we want to get the maximum value, we could use apply. Here, we are not assigning anything to the this keyword. So we just set that to null, then pass in our array. The bind method creates a new bound function, which wraps the original function object. So here we are essentially creating a new function bound to the object. Then we call the function along with our arguments. This has been a 90-second JavaScript January.
